The taxonomy is coarser than the underlying work in places - flagged in coverage_notes below.

'Other' contains Aflac's Data, Shared Engineering Excellence & Core IT RFP at EUR72.4M lost - the second-largest lost deal in the entire 2026 book, sitting in a catch-all category. This deserves its own look, not to be buried under 'Other' the way A&D's 'Unclassified' theme hid signal.

Underwriting Outcomes and Payment Modernization both show strong historical win rates (75% and 60% in 2025) but almost no 2026 activity - this is a pipeline-generation problem, not a client-specific whitespace, so it's handled in cross_cutting_patterns rather than forced into single-client records.

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Almost no AI deals despite universal carrier AI spending
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Six AI-related deals appeared in 2026 (zero in 2025); one won (EUR0.15M), four dropped at deal sizes as low as EUR0.02M-EUR0.05M (opening conversations, not real pursuits), one open. Of nine carriers profiled for how they actually buy AI (Allianz, AXA, Zurich, Liberty Mutual, Travelers, AIG, HSBC, USAA, plus the industry-wide claims layer), none bought an AI transformation programme from a systems integrator. Four built in-house (Allianz, Zurich, Travelers, USAA); the rest went direct to a model provider or hyperscaler (AXA-Microsoft, Liberty Mutual-OpenAI, Travelers-Anthropic, AIG-Anthropic/Palantir, HSBC-Mistral); claims point-solutions go to specialist insurtechs (Tractable, Shift Technology, EvolutionIQ), not SIs.
cross_cutting_patterns.source: Evident AI Index 2026; individual carrier company announcements

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Claims: bidding more, winning far less
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Deal count rose 67% (6 to 10 deals) year over year while money won fell 77% (EUR133.0M to EUR30.5M); win count fell from 2 to 1. Claims represents 60-80% of every premium dollar industry-wide - the single biggest AI opportunity in the sector. At two of the lost accounts, the carrier had already built the capability before Capgemini bid (Allianz, Zurich).
cross_cutting_patterns.source: Insurance Business Magazine; Decerto 2026 Claims Guide; Evident AI Index 2026

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Stopped selling the two best-performing offerings
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Payment Modernization (5 deals, 3 won, 60% win rate in 2025) and Underwriting Outcomes (4 deals, 3 won, 75% win rate in 2025) both dropped to near-zero 2026 activity (Payment Modernization: 0 deals; Underwriting Outcomes: 2 deals worth EUR0.85M open) despite live client references (AmFam Payments x2, Hiscox Payments Platform, Liberty Mutual Claims Billing EUR6.69M, Liberty Mutual Underwriting EUR23.13M, Zurich PEGA Underwriting EUR3.68M). This is a pipeline-generation problem, not a client- or technology-specific gap - nobody decided to stop selling these, pipeline generation followed the big core-system deals and nothing backfilled underneath.
cross_cutting_patterns.source: Internal deal data only - no external source needed

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Win once, then lose contact
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Only 12 of 40 clients with 2025 activity reappear in 2026. Nine clients with 2025 wins have zero 2026 activity - EUR209.8M of work with no follow-on. Dai-ichi Life (INS-09) is the one case with a documented, benign explanation (a BOT contract). The remaining eight - Grange Mutual (EUR11.28M), Generali (EUR3.50M), Prudential, Farmers, Hiscox, TruStage, and Nationwide - have no equivalent explanation found yet; the original churn read stands for these.

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Zero wins on cloud or mainframe bids
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Ten cloud or mainframe bids across two years (2025-2026). Zero wins.

cross_cutting_patterns.title: Small deals rarely grow into bigger ones
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: Roughly two-thirds of deals under EUR0.5M are lost, and the ones that are won leave no visible trail into a larger follow-on project.

cross_cutting_patterns.title: DXC Technology is a named, recurring incumbent across separate accounts
cross_cutting_patterns.detail: DXC Technology holds roughly 60% of Guardian Life's application development (INS-12) and is confirmed as MassMutual's actual mainframe-to-AWS-cloud migration partner (INS-19) - two independent, separately-sourced confirmations in the same batch of 10 accounts researched. Worth tracking as a named competitor across the wider Insurance book rather than treating each sighting as an isolated account-level finding.
cross_cutting_patterns.source: CIO Dive (Guardian Life); DXC Technology customer case study (MassMutual)
